title: stabilize-language-bindings-and-automate-deprecation-paths
creator: Rohan Mehta
description: Coordinated dependency bumps and API surface cleanup across Python, JS, and Go clients to remove legacy query params and unstable adapters. Goal: reduce maintenance overhead, improve runtime compatibility after kernel/runtime changes in runtime-1.21, and provide an automated migration path (codemods + docs) for customers. Scope includes: pinning critical transitive deps, removing deprecated request fields from SDKs, adding runtime compatibility tests, and publishing migration guides and automated codemods for each language binding.
acceptance_criteria: All three language clients (python, javascript, go) compile and run their test suites against runtime-1.21 with pinned deps and no deprecation warnings from our public API surface
Deprecated request fields (legacy_query_params, legacy_stream_flag) removed from public SDK surfaces with backward-compatible wrappers for one minor release
Automated codemod scripts published for python and javascript that convert 95% of existing call sites in internal repos; migration guide published for Go
CI matrix updated to run cross-language contract tests (end-to-end against a canary runtime) on every client PR
Customer-facing migration docs and deprecation timeline posted in the docs site and linked in SDK release notes
tasks: Audit top 50 transitive deps in python/js/go and identify incompatibility risks
Create and land dep-pin proposals and renovate PRs for each client
Introduce compatibility adapters (thin wrappers) that emit telemetry and deprecation warnings
Implement codemod for python (libcst) and javascript (jscodeshift); add sample runbook
Add cross-language compatibility tests to SDK e2e harness and CI matrix
Coordinate release notes and deprecation timeline with Docs + Support
Monitor canary usage and collect telemetry for migration blockers
comments: 2025-02-14 Rohan Mehta: Initial ticket created after runtime-1.21 kernel changes caused sporadic failures in the JS client. Scoped to dep pin + deprecations rather than full refactor.
2025-02-18 Sofia Chen: Ran audit across npm/pypi/gomod. Found 6 risky transitive deps (json-stream, http2 shim, proto-compat). Added to task list.
2025-02-21 Design review (Anita Gomez): Recommend keeping wrapper names stable and adding explicit migration examples in docs. Design will review codemod output for readability.
2025-02-26 Eng sync: Decided to land compatibility adapters for one major+two minor releases. Marked ENG-33107 as dependent for python auth changes.

2025-03-01 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-client/pull/214 - pins deps, adds deprecation wrapper. Notes: test failures on older python versions; planned to drop py3.7 support in a follow-up.

2025-03-04 QA report (Lina Ortiz): JS codemod converted 78% of call sites in internal dashboard repo. Remaining 22% require manual edits for custom wrappers. Adding task for manual migration assistance.
2025-03-05 Sofia Chen: Updated acceptance criteria with 95% codemod conversion target and added CI contract tests requirement.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Breaking changes for advanced customers who depended on legacy fields. Mitigation: compatibility wrappers + clear deprecation timeline + opt-in strict mode
Risk: Codemod false-positives for bespoke call wrappers. Mitigation: include dry-run flag, produce patch files, and provide manual migration support tickets
Risk: Test flakiness due to canary runtime instability. Mitigation: run cross-runner tests against both canary and stable runtimes and gate rollout on stability metrics
notes: Schedule a blocker review if customer-reported failures exceed 3 high-severity incidents during canary. Coordinate with Support to proactively reach out to top-10 customers using legacy fields.
